title: Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit
book_title: The Scoreboard: ARR, Retention, Rule of 40, and Promises Kept

epigraph.quote: In subscription software, revenue is a lagging echo; net new ARR, gross retention, and guidance credibility are the leading indicators.
epigraph.author: SaaS Operating Playbook

web_blocks.html: AvePoint's operational metrics from FY2023 through Q3 2026 (ended September 30, 2026) show simultaneous gains in scale and profit [2, 3]. Total ARR grew from $264.5M in FY2023 to $327.0M in FY2024 and $416.8M in FY2025 (+27% YoY) [2, 7]. By Q3 2026, ARR reached $495.1M (+27% YoY, +25% FX-adjusted), led by a record $30M in quarterly net new ARR (+34% YoY) [3]. Up-market traction is equally clear. Customers generating >$100,000 in ARR rose from 666 in FY2024 to 826 in FY2025, reaching 976 by Q3 2026 (+18% in nine months) [3, 7]. That six-figure cohort now anchors long-term enterprise expansion across all three Confidence Platform suites [3, 7].

web_blocks.caption: AvePoint Leading Operational KPIs (FY2023 – Q3 2026)
rows: Rule of 40 (ARR Growth + Non-GAAP Op Margin)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every core SaaS health indicator—NRR (112%), GRR (90%), Rule of 40 (44%), and $100K+ customer count (976)—improved sequentially through Q3 2026.

web_blocks.html: Two KPIs merit closer inspection. First, Gross Retention Rate (GRR) long sat in the 87%–88% range—solid for mid-market software, but below elite 93%–95% enterprise peers. One-time migration churn in Modernization and SMB seat trims drove that gap. In Q3 2026, however, GRR stepped up to 90% while NRR rose to 112% [3]. Multi-suite bundling (Resilience plus Control) is clearly cutting logo churn [3]. Second, management defines Rule of 40 as ARR growth (%) plus Non-GAAP operating margin (%) [7]. That score climbed from 31% in FY2023 to 38% in FY2024 and 44%–45% in FY2025–Q3 2026 [3, 7]. Even on a stricter FCF-margin plus revenue-growth basis (~19% plus 27% = 46%), AvePoint clears the bar. This margin gain came without starving R&D ($52.6M in FY2025) or cutting support. Higher SaaS mix (80.5% in Q3 2026), channel productivity, and cross-selling drove the leverage [2, 3, 7].

Disaggregating Net New ARR and cohort expansion confirms growth does not rely on one-off migrations. In Q3 2026, record net new ARR of $30M (+34% YoY) coincided with SaaS reaching 80.5% of total revenue ($105.5M of $131.1M) [3]. Implied NRR expansion (~11%–12% of beginning ARR) supplied roughly two-fifths of annual ARR additions [3]. New enterprise logos and MSP tenant onboarding via Elements supplied the rest. That drove $100K+ ARR accounts up by 150 net additions in nine months (826 to 976) [3, 7]. Multi-suite attach rates continue to climb as Resilience buyers add Control modules for Copilot and AI agent governance [7, 8]. Moving GRR from 88% in FY2025 to 90% in Q3 2026 also cuts annual churn leakage [2, 3]. Lower logo churn means the same cross-sell pace lifts net retention with less new-logo acquisition cost. Sustained >50% MSP ARR growth and rising $100K+ enterprise cohorts give AvePoint balanced momentum across both market tiers [3, 7].

Management's Q3 2026 commentary on November 5, 2026 underscored both demand breadth and AI monetization discipline [3]. CEO Dr. Tianyi Jiang stated: "Q3 was another strong quarter for AvePoint, as broad-based customer demand drove record net new ARR and an acceleration in total ARR growth for the second straight quarter, as well as further GAAP operating margin expansion." [3] He added that strong execution and cash generation let AvePoint "strategically invest in the largest market opportunity in our company's history: AI trust." [3] On the same call, CFO Jim Caci noted that AvePoint licenses AgentPulse based on employee counts rather than the number of agents managed [3]. That per-employee model gives enterprises predictable cost scaling as autonomous agent usage expands across departments [3].

web_blocks.title: Structural Potential: The $1B ARR by 2029 Runway
paragraphs: Reaching $1.0B ARR by FY2029 from $416.8M at year-end 2025 requires a 24.5% four-year CAGR [2, 7]. Q3 2026 ARR already sits at $495.1M (+27% YoY) [3]. Microsoft 365 Copilot and AI agent governance (AgentPulse) are driving multi-module cross-sells across tens of thousands of tenants [7, 8]. That runway is credible if NRR holds above 110% and APAC/EMEA budgets remain steady [3, 7].

Management's execution credibility also holds on a constant-currency basis. In Q3 2026, reported vs. FX-adjusted ARR growth differed by just 200 bps (27% vs. 25%) [3]. Reported NRR was 112% vs. 111% FX-adjusted, confirming organic demand rather than currency tailwinds [3]. Adding 150 net new $100K+ ARR accounts in nine months (826 to 976) shows strong up-market wallet share alongside MSP channel growth [3, 7]. Steady 25%–27% ARR compounding alongside margin gains validates management's conservative guidance cadence [2, 3, 7]. Holding GRR at 90%+ while scaling Elements MSP tenants gives AvePoint two clean levers to bridge the ~$505M gap to $1B by 2029 without dilutive mega-M&A [3, 7, 9]. Watch two quarterly indicators closely: $100K+ customer additions holding 40+ net adds per quarter, and NRR staying at or above 110% [3, 7].

book_paragraphs: In software, you and I should always look past management's press-release adjectives and check the operational scoreboard. AvePoint's scoreboard from FY2023 through Q3 2026 is remarkably clean. Annual Recurring Revenue has marched from $264.5 million in 2023 to $327.0 million in 2024, $416.8 million in 2025, and $495.1 million as of September 30, 2026—a steady 26% to 27% annual clip even as the base nearly doubled.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Quality Inside Retention and Cohort Expansion
paragraphs: Raw ARR growth can be bought temporarily with aggressive discounting, so we always inspect retention and cohort quality underneath it. For years, the one yellow flag in AvePoint's KPIs was Gross Retention Rate, which hovered around 87% to 88%. That is respectable for mid-market software, yet below the 93% to 95% benchmark of elite infrastructure systems—largely because one-off migration projects in the Modernization Suite naturally roll off once a tenant move finishes, and smaller SMB accounts occasionally trim seats.

Watch what happened in 2026. In Q2 2026, GRR ticked up to 89%, and in Q3 2026 it stepped up again to 90%, while Dollar-Based Net Retention Rate climbed to 112% reported (111% FX-adjusted). At the exact same time, the count of large enterprise customers paying more than $100,000 a year jumped from 666 at year-end 2024 to 826 at year-end 2025, and surged to 976 by Q3 2026—150 net new $100K+ accounts in just nine months. That combination tells us AvePoint is winning multi-suite platform expansions rather than relying on transactional migration spikes.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Rule of 40 Definition
paragraphs: Management tracks the Rule of 40 by adding ARR growth percentage to Non-GAAP operating margin percentage. On that basis, AvePoint progressed from 31% in FY2023 to 38% in FY2024, 45%+ in FY2025, and 44% on a trailing twelve-month basis in Q3 2026. Because Non-GAAP operating margin excludes stock-based compensation, a skeptical analyst should always cross-check the Rule of 40 using GAAP Free Cash Flow margin plus GAAP revenue growth. On that stricter test in FY2025—19.1% Free Cash Flow margin plus 27.0% revenue growth—AvePoint still scores 46%, clearing the bar cleanly without accounting sleight of hand.

book_subsections.title: The CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit and the 2029 $1 Billion Target
paragraphs: Just as reassuring is the CEO Walk-the-Talk Audit. Over three consecutive fiscal years—2023, 2024, and 2025—TJ Jiang and CFO Jim Caci set initial guidance that looked conservative, raised it mid-year, and beat the raised numbers by year-end. In 2023, they guided to $255–$261 million in ARR and delivered $264.5 million; in 2024, they targeted ~$317–$322 million and delivered $327.0 million while turning GAAP operating income positive ahead of schedule; in 2025, they delivered $416.8 million ARR at the top of their raised corridor alongside $35.1 million in GAAP net income. Their public goal of $1 billion in ARR by 2029 requires roughly a 24.5% four-year compound growth rate from 2025. Sitting at $495.1 million in Q3 2026 with record $30 million quarterly net new ARR, they are tracking ahead of schedule.

Let us unpack how realistic that $1 billion ARR milestone actually is by decomposing the math. Starting from $495.1 million in Q3 2026, AvePoint needs roughly $505 million of net new ARR over the next thirteen quarters—an average of $39 million per quarter, or ~21%–24% annual compounding. Notice the two engines doing the heavy lifting. First, at 112% Net Retention Rate, AvePoint's existing customer base automatically generates ~$55–$60 million of expansion ARR in the coming twelve months before a single new customer is signed. Second, the MSP channel—which grew 55% to $62 million in FY2025—gives AvePoint a scalable mid-market acquisition machine that does not require linear increases in direct sales headcount.

Where could that walk-the-talk streak break? Watch three leading indicators every quarter: Gross Retention Rate staying at or above 90%, $100K+ ARR customer additions maintaining a pace of 40–50+ net new accounts per quarter, and Copilot / AgentPulse attach rates translating into sustained 110%+ NRR. If any of those three KPIs slips, the 2029 $1 billion target will require heavier M&A—which, as we saw with Carbonite, is where software compounders get into trouble.

There is one more subtle KPI check you and I should perform: currency and constant-currency divergence. Because nearly 60% of AvePoint's GAAP revenue comes from EMEA and APAC, foreign-exchange swings can flatter or mask underlying demand. In Q3 2026, reported ARR grew 27% year-over-year while FX-adjusted ARR grew 25%; reported NRR was 112% while FX-adjusted NRR was 111%. Notice how tight that spread is—one to two percentage points—meaning AvePoint's 25%–27% growth and 111%–112% net retention are overwhelmingly organic, constant-currency operational execution rather than currency luck. When a management team delivers consistent beats across both reported and FX-adjusted metrics, their forecasting systems are genuinely dialed in.

Finally, consider what happens to operational leverage if AvePoint maintains a 44% to 46% Rule of 40 profile over the next three years. As ARR scales from $495 million toward $1 billion, every incremental point of gross retention—moving from 88% in FY2025 to 90% in Q3 2026 and potentially 92% over time—compounds lifetime customer value without requiring a single extra dollar of customer acquisition spend. That quiet retention improvement is often the highest-ROI lever in enterprise SaaS.

Put yourself in the shoes of an institutional auditor reviewing TJ Jiang's track record. In software, anyone can set an aspirational five-year ARR target at an Investor Day. What earns credibility is hitting initial annual guideposts, raising them mid-year without sacrificing gross retention, and expanding GAAP operating margins simultaneously. Across 2023, 2024, 2025, and the first three quarters of 2026, AvePoint has passed that operational walk-the-talk test every single year.

Still, disciplined underwriting requires asking what could derail the next three years of execution. Two operational watchpoints stand out: first, whether enterprise IT procurement cycles lengthen if macro budgets tighten in Europe or North America; and second, whether MSPs continue adopting multi-module Elements packages at the 55% growth pace seen in FY2025. Monitoring quarterly net new ARR ($30 million in Q3 2026) alongside GRR (90%) gives us an early-warning radar well before any slowdown hits GAAP revenue.

One final detail on the $100K+ ARR customer cohort deserves your attention: reaching 976 accounts in Q3 2026—up from 666 in FY2024 and 826 in FY2025—proves that AvePoint is successfully graduating mid-market and enterprise customers into six-figure annual commitments. When a single hospital network or university expands from basic backup into governance and analytics, its annual contract value climbs steadily, anchoring both NRR above 110% and long-term earnings visibility.

Put all of these KPIs side by side—$495.1 million ARR, 27% year-over-year growth, 90% gross retention, 112% net retention, 976 enterprise accounts above $100K ARR, a 44% Rule of 40 score, and three consecutive years of beat-and-raise guidance—and you have one of the cleanest operational scoreboards in mid-cap enterprise software. The numbers do not rely on aggressive adjustments or one-time spikes; they reflect steady, repeatable execution across direct enterprise sales and a rapidly scaling MSP channel.

As you track AvePoint over the coming quarters, keep your eye on the interplay between Net Retention Rate and Gross Retention Rate. Moving GRR from 88% to 90% in Q3 2026 means fewer dollars leak out the bottom of the bucket each year, so the same cross-sell velocity in AI governance and backup storage immediately lifts NRR and reduces the sales effort required to hit $1 billion in ARR by 2029.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A 90% GRR and 112% NRR paired with a 44% Rule of 40 score places AvePoint in the upper quartile of mid-cap enterprise SaaS. The key test over the next eight quarters is whether AI governance products like AgentPulse keep NRR above 110% as the legacy migration tailwind normalizes.
